module_title: ICJ Jurisdiction, Treaty Formation & 2026 BBNJ Milestone
introduction: This intermediate tier dissects the jurisdiction of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and the procedural mechanics of treaty-making (Signature vs. Ratification, Reservations). It highlights the massive 2026 High Seas Treaty milestone.

core_concepts.title: International Court of Justice (ICJ): Contentious Jurisdiction
core_concepts.description:
The ICJ settles legal disputes submitted to it by States.
- ONLY States may be parties in contentious cases (Individuals or NGOs cannot sue at the ICJ).
- The Consent Principle: The ICJ cannot automatically try a state. A state must **consent** to the Court's jurisdiction. Consent is given via:
  1. Special Agreement (Compromis): Two states agree to submit a specific dispute.
  2. Compromissory Clause: A clause in a treaty stating disputes will go to the ICJ.
  3. Optional Clause (Art 36(2)): States make a pre-emptive declaration accepting compulsory jurisdiction against any other state that makes the same declaration (Principle of Reciprocity).

core_concepts.title: Treaty Mechanics: Signature vs. Ratification
core_concepts.description:
Signing a treaty is often just the first step.
- Signature: Authenticates the text and expresses a willingness to continue the process. It does NOT automatically bind the state, but creates an obligation 'not to defeat the object and purpose' of the treaty before ratification (Art 18 VCLT).
- Ratification: The formal, legally binding step where the State confirms its consent to be bound, usually after getting approval from its domestic parliament.

core_concepts.title: Reservations to Treaties (Art 19 VCLT)
core_concepts.description:
A unilateral statement made by a State when ratifying a treaty, whereby it purports to exclude or modify the legal effect of certain provisions of the treaty in their application to that State.
- Rule: Reservations are allowed UNLESS the treaty explicitly prohibits them, or the reservation is **incompatible with the object and purpose** of the treaty.

core_concepts.title: Contemporary Milestone: The BBNJ Treaty (High Seas Treaty) 2026
core_concepts.description:
A highly testable current affairs and international law update.
- The Agreement on Marine Biological Diversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) officially **entered into force on January 17, 2026**, after reaching the required 60 ratifications in late 2025. 
- Significance: It brings the 'High Seas' (areas outside any nation's jurisdiction) under a legally binding conservation framework, implementing Area-Based Management Tools (MPAs) and regulating Marine Genetic Resources.

important_entities.name: ICJ Advisory Jurisdiction (Article 65)
important_entities.description: The ICJ can give an Advisory Opinion on any legal question at the request of the UNGA, UNSC, or other authorized UN organs. Unlike contentious cases, Advisory Opinions are fundamentally **non-binding**; they carry immense moral and legal weight but do not legally force states to act.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a question asks: 'Can the ICJ sentence a dictator to prison for war crimes?' **NO**. The ICJ resolves disputes between *States* (e.g., Ukraine v. Russia). Individual criminal responsibility is handled by the **International Criminal Court (ICC)**, which is an entirely separate entity governed by the Rome Statute, not the UN Charter.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The three primary ways a state submits to the jurisdiction of the World Court.

exam_strategy_tips: For current affairs integrated with legal theory, be prepared to answer questions on the **BBNJ Agreement**, noting its entry into force in **January 2026** as a landmark extension of the UNCLOS framework.
